newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTO ONE POINT SHORT OF PORTUGUESE TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTO ONE POINT SHORT OF PORTUGUESE TITLE.

text.p: Brazilian striker Mario Jardel scored twice in Porto's 2-1 home win over Belenenses on Sunday to put the reigning champions one point short of claiming a record third straight title.
Sporting, who beat Chaves 2-0 at home on Sunday, consolidated second place in the championship over their Lisbon rivals Benfica who lost 2-0 away to Maritimo on Saturday.
With four games to go, Porto lead with 76 points, followed by Sporting with 65 and Benfica with 55.

Jardel was the key to breaking past the well-organised Belenenses defences. Porto had to wait until the 58th minute before Jardel, the top scorer in the championship, scored with a header after a cross from the right by compatriot Artur Oliveira.
Six minutes later, Jardel sealed the victory with a powerful shot from just outside the penalty area, his 26th goal in the championship.
Belenenses scored a consolation 10 minutes from time.
Two goals in the first half guaranteed Sporting's win against Chaves. In the 16th minute striker Pedro Barbosa scored from a goalmouth scramble.
In the 39th minute, Chaves defender Paulo Alexandre scored an own goal.
Chaves's defender Antonio Tito was sent off for bookable offences in the 67th minute.

Benfica, who have played some of their worst soccer in living memory this season, lost for the first time in 18 years away against Maritimo. Their best chance to save face will be in the final of the Cup next month.
Maritimo's Brazilian striker Edmilson Lucena scored both goals against Benfica, in the 41st and 64th minutes.

Benfica, who were reduced to 10 men in the 72nd minute after the expulsion of captain Joao Pinto for two bookable offences, lost a chance to score a consolation two minutes from the final whistle. A free kick by Colombian defender Jorge Bermudez hit Maritimo's bar.
